dish: Hakodate shio ramen — whole-chicken & Minami-kayabe kombu clear broth, house-made thin noodles
n: Hakodate Men'ya Ichimonji, Yunokawa (函館麺や 一文字)
w: Yunokawa's shio-ramen specialist — a double soup of whole chicken and Minami-kayabe kombu, clam and shijimi essence in the salt tare, and its own thin straight noodles.

dish: British afternoon tea set in the old consulate
n: Tearoom Victorian Rose, Former British Consulate (ティールーム ヴィクトリアンローズ)
w: The English tearoom inside the 1913 Former British Consulate — antiques shipped from Britain, scones and a full afternoon-tea stand in Motomachi.

dish: the 'Ryūhō' yatai-style original Hakodate shio ramen of ~40 years ago
n: Shin-Hakodate Ramen Mame-san (新函館ラーメン マメさん)
w: Hōrai-chō counter reviving the shio ramen of the old 'Ryūhō' street stall (with its trademark fu) — the 'phantom' Hakodate bowl was guest-revived at the Shin-Yokohama Ramen Museum.

n: Indo Curry Koike Honten, Hakodate (印度カレー 小いけ本店)
w: Founded 1948, Hakodate's old-school curry house — a sharply spiced, nostalgic roux that locals rank beside Gotōken's.

dish: chefs' market seafood — squid, kaisendon at the in-market shokudō
n: Hakodate Jiyū Ichiba (はこだて自由市場)
w: The locals' and chefs' market rather than the tourists' — sushi chefs buy here; fish stalls will slice what you pick, plus a shokudō and food court.

dish: kaisendon, uni-ikura-don and ikasōmen from the market canteens
n: Donburi Yokochō Ichiba, Hakodate Morning Market (どんぶり横丁市場)
address: Wakamatsu-chō, Hakodate, Hokkaido, Japan (inside Hakodate Morning Market)
w: The Morning Market's canteen arcade — a covered lane of donburi shokudō open from dawn into lunch, the place for kaisendon by Hakodate Station.

dish: shiratama matcha-cream anmitsu and the Hishii parfait in a 1921 pawnshop kura
w: Hakodate's pioneering renovation café — a 1921 pawnbroker's warehouse, Western counter downstairs, tatami upstairs, Japanese sweets and an antique shop.

n: Sabō Kyū Chayatei, Suehiro-chō (茶房 旧茶屋亭)
address: Suehiro-chō, Hakodate, Hokkaido, Japan (near Kanemori Red Brick Warehouses)
w: A 1939 merchant house — a designated Traditional Building of Cultural Significance — where the tea-ceremony-trained owner whisks matcha cup by cup.

dish: ranchiri soba (egg-bound), kashiwa-nuki and green-tea soba
n: Chikurōen Azumaya Sōhonten, Kushiro (竹老園 東家総本店)
w: Meiji-founded soba house in a 1927 building with a Japanese garden — the origin of Kushiro's green-tinged soba, served as ranchiri, kashiwa-nuki and soba-zushi.

dish: Kushiro robatayaki — local saba and Notsuke scallops grilled over charcoal
n: Robata Renga, Kushiro (炉ばた 煉瓦)
w: Robatayaki in a late-Meiji red-brick grain-and-salt warehouse by Fisherman's Wharf MOO — Kushiro-landed fish and Notsuke scallops grilled at your table.

dish: Nemuro escalope — pork cutlet on bamboo-shoot butter rice with demi-glace
n: Shokuji to Kissa Dorian, Nemuro (食事と喫茶 どりあん)
address: Nemuro, Hokkaido, Japan (7 min walk from JR Nemuro Station)
w: Since 1969 the reference escalope — butter rice, pork cutlet and demi-glace — plus its 'Oriental rice', 7 minutes' walk from Nemuro Station.

dish: Okhotsk Beer — Hokkaido's first craft beer, pilsner & ales on tap
n: Okhotsk Beer Factory, Kitami (オホーツクビアファクトリー)
w: The brewpub that started Hokkaido's craft-beer boom — all-malt pilsner and ales brewed on site in Kitami, with a restaurant.

dish: Utoro-caught sashimi teishoku (uni, botan-ebi) and the 'Araiso-don'
n: Araiso Ryōri Kuma no Ya, Utoro (荒磯料理 熊の家)
address: 187-11 Utoro-nishi, Shari, Shari District, Hokkaido, Japan
w: Utoro's local-catch-only fish house — 5–7 kinds of sashimi including sea urchin and botan shrimp; a green-lantern (local produce) restaurant.

dish: Utoro salmon and summer uni teishoku, pick-your-own kaisendon
n: Oshokujidokoro Ezogashima, Utoro (お食事処 夷知床)
address: Utoro, Shari, Shari District, Hokkaido, Japan
w: Utoro diner built around the town's two catches — salmon set meals and, in summer, Utoro uni; build-your-own seafood bowls.

dish: home-raised Shiraoi-beef burger and Shiraoi-beef curry
n: Farm Restaurant Uemura Base, Shiraoi (ファームレストラン ウエムラ・ベース)
address: 109-20 Ishiyama, Shiraoi, Shiraoi District, Hokkaido, Japan
w: Run by one of Hokkaido's few birth-to-finish Kuroge-wagyu farms (Uemura Bokujō) — Shiraoi-beef burgers, reopened 2021.

dish: charcoal yakiniku and steak of Shiraoi beef
n: Yakiniku & Steak Restaurant Cowbell, Shiraoi (レストラン カウベル)
address: 112-14 Ishiyama, Shiraoi, Shiraoi District, Hokkaido, Japan
w: Butcher-run since 1975 — Shiraoi-beef yakiniku over charcoal and steaks, listed among the town's Shiraoi-beef houses.

dish: farm-milk gelato with Mt Yōtei view; 'Mura-ichiban' curry
n: Lake Hill Farm, Tōyako (レークヒル・ファーム)
address: 127 Hanawa, Tōyako, Abuta District, Hokkaido, Japan
w: Dairy-farm gelateria on the hill above Lake Tōya — gelato made daily from its own cows' milk, looking across to Mt Yōtei.

dish: home-style teishoku of Funka Bay seafood and local produce
n: Meshidokoro Matsumaeya, Tōyako Onsen (めしどころ 松前屋)
address: 40-16 Tōyako Onsen, Tōyako, Abuta District, Hokkaido, Japan
w: Five minutes from the Tōyako Onsen bus terminal — the onsen town's local-ingredient set-meal house for seasonal seafood.
